subject: Streaming SLO probe pack and anchor measurements - post-call
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@edgemart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming SLO probe pack and anchor measurements - post-call

Hi Amelia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align the benchmark run and confirm whether our Dedicated offering will meet EdgeMart's latency and streaming constraints.

Recap (what we heard)
- Target user-facing latency: p95 <= 300ms for short replies (<= 32 tokens), p95 <= 800ms for longer streaming replies (200-400 tokens).
- Throughput expectation: 120 concurrent active users at peak, average session concurrency ~8 requests/s per region.
- Streaming requirement: partial tokens must begin flowing within 150-250ms; smooth token cadence (no >200ms gaps).
- Repro constraints: production traffic includes variable prompt lengths, high prefix reuse (70% repeated prefixes).

Deliverables we promised
1) A "probe pack" with: prompt seeds, traffic mix, target payload sizes, and an eval harness checklist. (attached: slo-probe-pack-v1.zip, prompt-seed-v3.json)
2) Measurement definitions and scripts for p50/p95/p99, token vs request latency, and streaming gap analysis (attached: eval-harness-instructions.md).
3) Suggested warmup and cache-warming policy to capture KV cache behavior in benchmarking.

Action items / asks from EdgeMart
- Please validate the two representative prompt groups in prompt-seed-v3.json ("checkout-flow" and "support-chat-short"). If you have an internal prompt set we should include, share a sanitized sample.
- Confirm target traffic window and time zone for the run (we penciled in 2028-06-14T22:00Z but can shift).
- Provide an internal contact for rate-limited auth/whitelist to run probes from your account.

Technical notes (short)
- Our harness will measure: server-side generation time (model forward/backward not applicable), pre-tokenization overhead, streaming first-byte latency, inter-token cadence, and queuing delay under continuous batching.
- We will log model variant + quantization profile + kernel selection for each run to ensure reproducibility.

Next step: If that looks right, we'll schedule a 30-minute sync with your platform eng (Amelia + platform@edgemart.com) and our infra lead (Rishi) to finalize the probe window and whitelist.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148

Attachments: slo-probe-pack-v1.zip (25KB stub), prompt-seed-v3.json (5KB stub), eval-harness-instructions.md (8KB stub)

From: Amelia Torres <amelia@edgemart.com>

Cc: EdgeMart Platform <platform@edgemart.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming SLO probe pack and anchor measurements - post-call

Thanks Ben — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- The p95 target for short replies is firm (<=300ms) — that is user-facing on our web checkout. Longer streaming replies are less strict but p95 <= 800ms is a good guardrail.
- Peak concurrency: our telemetry shows 100-140 concurrent websocket sessions during promotions; 120 is a reasonable planning figure.
- For streaming cadence: we care most about first-byte and the maximum token gap (we've seen vendor gaps of ~500ms that break client-side playback).

Two requests:
1) Can you include a rule to measure 'cold-start' vs 'steady-state' for a 10-minute window? We want to know how much warmup reduces latency for a high-reuse prefix.
2) Please include an optional run where the model is quantized to int8 (if supported) and note any config differences.

We'll send a sanitized set of 50 representative prompts and a replay script by EOD tomorrow. Our platform team can be available Tue 2028-06-14 22:00Z for the window you suggested.

--
Amelia
Amelia Torres | Head of Platform, EdgeMart
amelia@edgemart.com

Thanks — good asks. Short replies to both:

1) Cold-start vs steady-state: included. The probe pack contains a 10-minute cold-run and a 30-minute steady-state window; we will report both p50/p95/p99 and delta. We'll also capture prefix reuse ratio and KV cache hit rate.

2) Quantized runs: we can run int8 quantized variants; we will tag those runs and publish a per-token latency delta and any change in generation quality (we'll include Rouge/BLEU-ish checks for structural regressions).

A couple of additional technical checks from Rishi (cc'd):
- Please confirm whether you will accept our synthetic traffic over a whitelisted IP, or prefer to run the harness from within your VPC (we support both).
- For streaming, what client playback buffer do you use? (common values: 50ms/100ms/200ms) — helps us tune token chunk sizes for realistic cadence.

Attached: small update to the harness instructions that lists environment vars we will need.

If you're okay, we'll lock the window Tue 2028-06-14 22:00Z and Rishi will send a separate calendar invite for the 30-minute sync.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia@edgemart.com>
Date: 2028-06-09T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Streaming SLO probe pack and anchor measurements - post-call

Looping in a couple engineering notes we'll need to capture in the run plan (Amelia, you can ignore if TMI):

- Measurement definition:
  * request_latency_ms: time from HTTP request receipt to first token byte out (server-time).
  * generation_latency_ms: sum of model forward passes that produced tokens.
  * token_gap_ms: inter-token arrival gap at client socket. Measure max, median, and 95th percentile over run.
  * queue_delay_ms: time request spent waiting for batching/coalescing.

- Repro steps we will log: seed, tokenizer version, model sha, kernel selection, batch size, pad/truncate policy, KV cache warmup sequence. Please ensure the sanitizer you send keeps tokenization consistent.

- For the cold-start path: we'll start with an empty KV cache and measure the first 200 requests; for steady-state we will run a 10-minute warmup followed by the 30-minute measurement window.

- Success criteria proposal (for initial qualification): p95 short replies <= 300ms AND streaming first-byte <= 250ms for 90% of sessions during the peak window, with no >200ms token gaps for >95% of tokens. These are negotiable — we'll mark them as "qualification anchors" not hard SLAs.

I'll merge these notes into the harness instructions and push an updated pack by EOD. Ben — can you confirm whether we should capture client-side playback metrics or only server-side (we can add an optional JS playback harness if EdgeMart wants it)?

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel | Performance PM, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
